title: Water Management and Conservation
desc: Measure, save and manage water at home, farm, school or business, with leak checks, rainwater, reuse and fair sharing.
outcomes: Explain the water cycle and local water risks.
Do a water audit and leak test.
Judge quality, safety and cost of reuse.
Write a water-saving plan with targets.
task: Audit water use at one site, plan savings, design a rainwater or reuse option and set a measurable target.
condition: A real site or a practice case, a bucket and timer or meter, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Audit lists all uses in litres; leak test is documented; savings and payback are calculated; water safety rules are stated; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Facility managers, farmers, school staff, residents, community groups.
evidence: audit sheet, leak test record, plan, target
modules: Know where your water comes from and what could go wrong.
Rain, rivers, lakes, groundwater and storage.
Know your supply source, schedule and rules.
Cost and availability vary by season.
Find your supplier, tariff and quality report.
Know water-saving rules or limits in your area.
A town cuts supply in summer; households that store water cope better. A household learns its supply is cut for three hours a day and sizes storage for 150 L per person.
Describe your water supply and one risk. Add supply schedule and storage size.
Read the meter at the same time daily.
List uses: taps, toilets, showers, cleaning, irrigation, laundry.
Convert to litres per person per day.
A home uses 180 L per person per day; the benchmark target is 135 L. Garden use is 40 per cent of the summer total.
Do an audit for one week. Split your audit into indoor and outdoor.
Night meter test: stop all use, check the meter does not move.
A drip per second wastes thousands of litres per year.
Check taps, hoses, tanks and float valves.
Measure how fast a bucket fills to find flow rate.
A toilet leak is found with food dye and repaired with a new valve, saving 20 L per day. A leaking tank float is found after the meter moves at night, wasting 60 L per day.
Run a leak test and record results. Add a flow-rate test.
Aerators, efficient flushes, full loads, shorter showers.
Replace the worst offenders first: toilets, showers and garden hoses.
Give households a weekly target and feedback.
Aerators cut tap flow by 25 per cent. A low-flow shower head saves 6 L per minute.
Choose five measures and estimate savings. Rank measures by litres saved per rupee spent.
Roof area x rainfall x efficiency = litres per year.
First-flush diverter, filter and covered tank.
Add a mesh at gutters, a first-flush device and an overflow route.
A 100 m2 roof and 800 mm rain with 80 per cent efficiency gives about 64,000 L a year. A 5,000 L tank with a 100 m2 roof fills after about 60 mm of rain.
Design a system. Add tank cleaning and overflow plan.
Grey water and treatment need care.
Grey water from basins can irrigate non-edible plants with care.
Avoid contact with edible leaves where unsafe.
Never use untreated grey water on salad crops.
Use a simple sand and gravel filter before reuse where permitted.
Bath water irrigates ornamental plants but not salad crops. A school filters hand-wash water and uses it for flushing.
List safe uses and unsafe uses. Add a treatment step and test note.
Check soil moisture with a finger or a simple sensor.
Drip cuts water use by about 40 per cent compared with flood irrigation. Mulch and drip lines keep soil moist twice as long.
Plan a small plot. Add a watering timetable.
Set a target such as 20 litres per person per day saved.
Display progress where everyone can see.
A school sets a 20 per cent cut in one year. A notice board shows monthly litres saved by class.
Present the plan. Add a progress display design.
quiz: Litres per person per day?
Total use / people / days. (Covered in module 1: Water cycle and local risk. To pass that module: Sources named and risk explained.)
Night meter test?
No use but meter moves means a leak. (Covered in module 2: Water audit. To pass that module: Table complete.)
Rainwater formula?
Area x rain x efficiency. (Covered in module 3: Finding leaks. To pass that module: Result recorded with fix.)
Safe grey water use?
Irrigation of non-edible plants. (Covered in module 4: Saving at the tap. To pass that module: Savings estimated with numbers.)
Aerator benefit?
Reduces flow. (Covered in module 5: Rainwater harvesting. To pass that module: Calculation correct.)
Why first flush?
Removes dirt. (Covered in module 6: Reuse and water quality. To pass that module: Rules clear.)
Mulch use?
Keeps moisture. (Covered in module 7: Irrigation and farming. To pass that module: Plan complete.)
Drinking water rule?
Treat and test. (Covered in module 8: Plan and target. To pass that module: Target measurable.)
Why meters?
To measure savings. (Covered in module 8: Plan and target. To pass that module: Target measurable.)
Why share plan?
Community buy-in. (Covered in module 8: Plan and target. To pass that module: Target measurable.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others

ladder: Water cycle and local risk

L1: learner can name water sources. Focus module: Water cycle and local risk (Understand, 3 h). Know where your water comes from and what could go wrong. Key points: Rain, rivers, lakes, groundwater and storage. Droughts, floods and quality problems. Know your supply source, schedule and rules. Cost and availability vary by season. Find your supplier, tariff and quality report. Know water-saving rules or limits in your area.

Teach: open with the worked example. A town cuts supply in summer; households that store water cope better. A household learns its supply is cut for three hours a day and sizes storage for 150 L per person. Then set the activity: Describe your water supply and one risk. Add supply schedule and storage size. Mark against the standard: Sources named and risk explained. Check at this level: Litres per person per day? Model answer: Total use / people / days.
Water audit

L2: learner knows leak basics. Focus module: Water audit (Apply, 5 h). Measure first. Key points: Read the meter at the same time daily. List uses: taps, toilets, showers, cleaning, irrigation, laundry. Convert to litres per person per day. Compare with benchmarks. Compare winter and summer readings. Separate indoor and outdoor use.

Teach: open with the worked example. A home uses 180 L per person per day; the benchmark target is 135 L. Garden use is 40 per cent of the summer total. Then set the activity: Do an audit for one week. Split your audit into indoor and outdoor. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: Night meter test? Model answer: No use but meter moves means a leak.
Finding leaks

L3: learner can audit. Focus module: Finding leaks (Apply, 4 h). Small drips cost a lot. Key points: Night meter test: stop all use, check the meter does not move. Dye test for toilets. A drip per second wastes thousands of litres per year. Fix quickly. Check taps, hoses, tanks and float valves. Measure how fast a bucket fills to find flow rate.

Teach: open with the worked example. A toilet leak is found with food dye and repaired with a new valve, saving 20 L per day. A leaking tank float is found after the meter moves at night, wasting 60 L per day. Then set the activity: Run a leak test and record results. Add a flow-rate test. Mark against the standard: Result recorded with fix. Check at this level: Rainwater formula? Model answer: Area x rain x efficiency.
Saving at the tap

L4: learner can fix and save. Focus module: Saving at the tap (Analyse, 4 h). Cheap measures work. Key points: Aerators, efficient flushes, full loads, shorter showers. Behaviour and signs. Track savings. Maintenance matters. Replace the worst offenders first: toilets, showers and garden hoses. Give households a weekly target and feedback.

Teach: open with the worked example. Aerators cut tap flow by 25 per cent. A low-flow shower head saves 6 L per minute. Then set the activity: Choose five measures and estimate savings. Rank measures by litres saved per rupee spent. Mark against the standard: Savings estimated with numbers. Check at this level: Safe grey water use? Model answer: Irrigation of non-edible plants.
Rainwater harvesting

L5: learner can design rainwater. Focus module: Rainwater harvesting (Create, 5 h). Catch and store rain. Key points: Roof area x rainfall x efficiency = litres per year. First-flush diverter, filter and covered tank. Use for non-drinking unless treated. Maintain tanks. Add a mesh at gutters, a first-flush device and an overflow route. Clean the tank every year.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 100 m2 roof and 800 mm rain with 80 per cent efficiency gives about 64,000 L a year. A 5,000 L tank with a 100 m2 roof fills after about 60 mm of rain. Then set the activity: Design a system. Add tank cleaning and overflow plan. Mark against the standard: Calculation correct. Check at this level: Aerator benefit? Model answer: Reduces flow.
Irrigation and farming

L6: learner can lead a plan. Focus module: Irrigation and farming (Apply, 3 h). Use less, grow more. Key points: Drip lines, mulching, timing. Soil moisture checks. Crop choice for local rain. Reduce evaporation. Check soil moisture with a finger or a simple sensor. Water early morning or evening.

Teach: open with the worked example. Drip cuts water use by about 40 per cent compared with flood irrigation. Mulch and drip lines keep soil moist twice as long. Then set the activity: Plan a small plot. Add a watering timetable. Mark against the standard: Plan complete. Check at this level: Why first flush? Model answer: Removes dirt.
Plan and target

L7: learner can audit others. Focus module: Plan and target (Create, 4 h). Make it stick. Key points: Targets, owners, dates. Report monthly. Share with the community. Celebrate wins. Set a target such as 20 litres per person per day saved. Display progress where everyone can see.

Teach: open with the worked example. A school sets a 20 per cent cut in one year. A notice board shows monthly litres saved by class. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Add a progress display design. Mark against the standard: Target measurable. Check at this level: Mulch use? Model answer: Keeps moisture.
